title: FEVER: a Large-scale Dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification
abstract: Introduces a large fact-verification dataset containing claims labeled Supported, Refuted, or NotEnoughInfo together with evidence sentences from Wikipedia. It provides an empirical framework for separating an asserted claim from independently retrieved textual evidence used to corroborate or refute it.
venue: Proceedings of the 2018 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies

admission.reason: FEVER is strong static evidence-based claim verification, but the abstract does not add longitudinal revision, source-relative lifecycle state, or workplace/operational communication. The corpus already has fact-verification evidence of the supported/refuted/insufficient-evidence pattern, so another generic Wikipedia verification benchmark does not close the current gaps.

title: Evidence-based Trustworthiness
abstract: Develops probabilistic models that jointly estimate source trustworthiness and claim credibility when multiple sources make assertions and provide evidence. The framework distinguishes directly asserted claims from claims inferred through noisy NLP processing and evaluates source- and evidence-aware credibility estimation.
venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

admission.reason: The multi-source trustworthiness and claim-credibility formulation is relevant to F3, but the abstract does not show longitudinal work-item revision, temporal state resolution, or operational communication. Its useful capability overlaps stronger verified F3 candidates in this set, and its identity is UNCHECKED.

title: FEVEROUS: Fact Extraction and VERification Over Unstructured and Structured information
abstract: Introduces a fact-verification dataset in which claims must be checked against evidence drawn from both Wikipedia sentences and table cells. Claims receive support, refutation, or insufficient-evidence labels, enabling empirical study of corroboration across heterogeneous evidence.
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, Datasets and Benchmarks Track

admission.reason: FEVEROUS extends fact verification to sentences and table cells, but its contribution is heterogeneous evidence verification rather than longitudinal state evolution or revision semantics. That structured-evidence extension does not materially close the Topic 06 gaps.

title: Improving Iterative Text Revision by Learning Where to Edit from Other Revision Tasks
abstract: Models iterative text revision as a process that detects editable spans, predicts edit intentions, and generates revised text. It transfers supervision from related revision datasets to improve identification of where and how a document should be revised.
venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

admission.reason: The paper uses edit intentions in an iterative revision system, but its central capability is locating and generating edits. It does not show classification of the semantic relationship between successive operational assertions, and the verified arXivEdits candidate provides more direct F9 evidence for version alignment plus edit-intent classification.

title: AVeriTeC: A Dataset for Real-world Claim Verification with Evidence from the Web
abstract: Introduces a dataset of real-world claims from fact-checking organizations with web evidence represented as question-answer pairs and textual justifications. The annotation procedure is designed to obtain sufficient contemporaneous evidence while reducing temporal leakage, supporting verification of claims against independently gathered sources.

admission.reason: AVeriTeC provides independent web evidence and explicitly reduces temporal leakage, but the abstract still describes static real-world claim verification rather than evolving work-item state, revision relations, or source-relative completion claims across successive communications. It therefore does not materially close the current longitudinal gaps.

title: User Edits Classification Using Document Revision Histories
abstract: Uses supervised learning over document revision histories to distinguish factual edits from fluency-oriented edits. Features include language-model probabilities, string similarity, part-of-speech information, named entities, and adaptive revision-history features.
venue: Proceedings of the 13th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics

admission.reason: The factual-versus-fluency edit distinction is too coarse for Topic 06's required semantic effects such as supersession, correction, supplementation, revocation, reopening, and conflict. It is also UNCHECKED and is dominated here by the verified arXivEdits F9 candidate with finer-grained edit intentions and explicit multi-version alignment.

title: Understanding Iterative Revision from Human-Written Text
abstract: Studies sequences of human-written revisions and introduces a corpus annotated with edit intentions across multiple domains. The work evaluates models that use distinctions among edit intentions to better understand and perform iterative text revision.
venue: Proceedings of the 60th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

admission.reason: The abstract supports F9 through multi-domain iterative revision and edit-intent annotation, but this contribution substantially overlaps the verified arXivEdits candidate, which additionally provides explicit multi-version document/sentence/word alignment. Given the identity is UNCHECKED and no distinct operational-communication capability is shown, it does not justify another reading slot.

title: Learning to Classify Email into “Speech Acts”
abstract: Presents supervised methods for classifying email according to sender intent using an ontology containing communicative acts such as proposing, committing, delivering, and requesting. The work is motivated by tracking the status of ongoing joint activities in workplace email.
venue: Proceedings of the 2004 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

admission.reason: This is highly relevant workplace email data, but the modeled capability is utterance-level speech-act classification such as proposing, committing, delivering, and requesting. That belongs primarily to Topic 05's utterance-time action/commitment extraction boundary; the abstract does not show classification of how later messages revise, supersede, contradict, or reopen earlier state.

title: One Document, Many Revisions: A Dataset for Classification and Description of Edit Intents
abstract: Introduces a dataset based on complete Wikipedia revision histories with edit-intent labels associated with individual revisions. The paper evaluates edit-intent classification and generation of natural-language descriptions of revisions, explicitly modeling iterative revision histories rather than isolated document pairs.
venue: Proceedings of the Thirteenth Language Resources and Evaluation Conference

admission.reason: Complete revision histories and edit-intent labels are relevant to F9, but the capability overlaps the verified arXivEdits candidate. The abstract does not add workplace communication or a revision ontology closer to supersession/correction/reopening, and the paper identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Fact or Fiction: Verifying Scientific Claims
abstract: Introduces SciFact, a dataset of scientific claims paired with abstracts containing evidence that supports or refutes them and annotated rationales. The work evaluates retrieval and reasoning models that verify claims against independently selected scientific evidence.
venue: Proceedings of the 2020 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

admission.reason: SciFact is a strong evidence-based claim-verification benchmark, but the abstract describes static scientific claims and independently selected evidence rather than longitudinal communication, changing factual state, or revision relations. Its F3 capability is already represented more directly by admitted candidates.

title: Neural Models of Factuality
abstract: Develops neural models for predicting the factuality of events described in text and evaluates them on multiple factuality datasets. The models estimate source-relative textual commitment rather than independently verified truth.
venue: Proceedings of the 2018 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies

admission.reason: The paper directly models source-relative event factuality and is relevant to F2, but the stated open gaps already acknowledge that admitted factuality literature establishes textual source commitment. This abstract does not add longitudinal revision, temporal ordering, independent corroboration, or operational-domain evaluation, so it duplicates an already-covered component rather than closing a current gap.

title: DeClarE: Debunking Fake News and False Claims using Evidence-Aware Deep Learning
abstract: Presents an evidence-aware neural model for assessing claim credibility using external evidence articles, textual signals, and information about source trustworthiness. The approach explicitly separates claims from supporting or contradicting evidence gathered from other sources.
venue: Proceedings of the 2018 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

admission.reason: DeClarE separates claims from external evidence and source trust signals, but the abstract does not show longitudinal state revision or operational communication. Its static evidence-aware credibility capability overlaps verified F3 candidates admitted here, and its identity is UNCHECKED.

title: MultiFC: A Real-World Multi-Domain Dataset for Evidence-Based Fact Checking of Claims
abstract: Introduces a multi-domain collection of real-world claims from fact-checking organizations together with textual evidence sources, metadata, and expert veracity judgments. The work evaluates models that jointly rank evidence pages and predict claim veracity.
venue: Proceedings of the 2019 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing and the 9th International Joint Conference on Natural Language Processing

admission.reason: MultiFC provides real-world evidence retrieval and veracity prediction across domains, but the abstract remains a static fact-checking setup. It does not evaluate successive revisions, lifecycle state, temporal ordering, or operational communication, and its F3 contribution is already covered more directly by admitted candidates.

title: Automatically Classifying Edit Categories in Wikipedia Revisions
venue: Proceedings of the 2013 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

admission.reason: No abstract is supplied, so the admission gate cannot determine whether the work merely labels generic Wikipedia edit categories or actually classifies semantic effects useful to F9 such as factual correction, reversal, supplementation, deletion, or other revision intent. The abstract or equivalent primary-paper summary is required to settle this.

title: DREAM: Classification Scheme for Dialog Acts in Clinical Research Query Mediation
abstract: Develops and empirically validates a dialog-act annotation scheme using email exchanges for clinical research data requests. The corpus contains task-oriented multi-message dialogues, and the taxonomy includes task-management and resolution states as well as backward-looking correction or suggestion acts.

admission.reason: The clinical-research email setting is valuable operational-domain evidence, and the taxonomy includes correction, suggestion, task-management, and resolution acts. However, the abstract describes dialog-act classification rather than maintaining a work item's longitudinal state or classifying explicit semantic relations between earlier and later observations. Domain vocabulary matches, but the required F1 capability is not established.

title: MEANTIME, the NewsReader Multilingual Event and Time Corpus
abstract: Introduces a multilingual corpus annotated for entities, events, temporal expressions, semantic roles, temporal relations, and event and entity coreference, including cross-document links. The resource supports research combining event identity and temporal organization across documents.
venue: Proceedings of the Tenth International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation

admission.reason: MEANTIME supports event identity, temporal relations, and cross-document links, but it is another news-derived event/time corpus rather than an operational longitudinal-state method. The existing gap explicitly identifies over-reliance on news evidence, so this would reinforce an already represented transfer setting without closing the workplace or revision-relation gaps.

title: LEDA: a Large-Organization Email-Based Decision-Dialogue-Act Analysis Dataset
abstract: Introduces a dialog-act dataset derived from real-world IETF mailing-list discussions about organizational decision making and trains transformer-based dialog-act classifiers. The annotation inventory includes action proposals, stated decisions, agreement, disagreement, information exchange, and clarification-related acts, and the analysis examines communication over the life cycle of decision discussions.
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2023

admission.reason: LEDA supplies valuable large-organization mailing-list dialogue and decision-life-cycle acts, but its modeled capability is dialog-act classification of proposals, decisions, agreement, disagreement, information exchange, and clarification. The abstract does not show longitudinal state maintenance or explicit classification of supersession, correction, revocation, reopening, or unresolved conflict, so it is closer to Topic 05 than the missing Topic 06 capability.

title: Fully Automated Fact Checking Using External Sources
abstract: Presents an automated fact-checking framework that searches for external sources and combines semantic text representations with estimates of source reliability. The method is evaluated on rumor detection and community question-answering fact-checking tasks.
venue: Proceedings of the International Conference Recent Advances in Natural Language Processing, RANLP 2017

admission.reason: The method gathers external sources and incorporates source reliability, so it is relevant to generic F3 claim verification. The abstract does not show longitudinal revision, source-relative work-item state, or operational communication, and stronger verified F3 candidates in this set cover dialogue verification and source-aware provenance. Its identity is also UNCHECKED.
